newsitem.title: JAPAN: North Korea says heatwave damages crops, economy.
newsitem.headline: North Korea says heatwave damages crops, economy.

text.p: Famine-stricken North Korea said on Tuesday that a record heatwave in July has seriously damaged crops and other parts of its hard-hit economy.

The state-run Korean Central News Agency (KCNA), in a report seen in Tokyo, said the average noon temperature in July was above 35 degrees Celsius (95 degrees Fahrenheit) in Pyongyang and some other areas.
It said temperatures were three to five degrees C higher than usual on average and more than ten degrees C higher in some places.
KCNA quoted Ri Jong-u, director of the Central Forecast Institute of the Hydro-Meteorological Service, as saying the heatwave was unprecedented in 61 years of weather observation.
"The drought from the high temperature is inflicting a serious damage on agriculture and other domains of the national economy," the KCNA report said.

"The bottoms of reservoirs were visible and thousands of rivers and streams had dried up. This seriously affected the growth of crops and made it impossible to supply industrial water through irrigation networks," it said.
The report said North Korea could not expect rain for some time.

Last week, Pyongyang said this year's heatwave and drought have had a "catastrophic" impact on its economy and worsened food shortages following two years of floods which devastated substantial areas of farmland.
North Korean officials have said they need some 800,000 tonnes of grain in emergency aid from foreign countries to ease food shortages until the next harvest in October.

The head of an international food aid organisation said in South Korea on Tuesday that at least five million people in North Korea are suffering from starvation on levels comparable to the Somalia and Ethiopia famines.
"It is a disaster in the making," Ted Yamamori, president of Food for the Hungry International, said in Seoul after visiting North Korea last week.
